context_requirements: Cells must be proliferating and dependent on Akt/mTOR and/or ERK signaling for survival.
Intact ER stress/UPR and autophagy machinery to engage nelfinavir/ritonavir responses.
For the strongest response, ER-positive or Akt-addicted lineage (e.g., MCF7).
Concentrations near 10 micromolar are required; lower exposures may give little transcriptional change.
falsifiers: No change in UPR/ER-stress landmark genes (e.g., DDIT4, DNAJB1, HERPUD1, XBP1) at 6 or 24 h in any line.
No depletion of proliferation/cell-cycle landmark transcripts (e.g., CCND1, CDK4, MCM3, TOP2A) at 24 h.
No CDKN1A induction or G1-arrest signature at 24 h.
Strong and uniform up-regulation of interferon-stimulated genes across all lines, which would suggest an antiviral rather than the expected metabolic/ER-stress mechanism.
Complete absence of any transcriptional response in MCF7 and A549, the lines most expected to respond.

evidence.supports: Nelfinavir and other HIV protease inhibitors inhibit proliferation and induce ER stress, autophagy, and apoptosis in NSCLC and NCI60 lines.
Ritonavir causes G1 arrest, depletes cyclin D1, CDK2/4/6, phospho-Rb and phospho-Akt, and inhibits breast cancer growth in vitro and in vivo.
Ritonavir inhibits endothelial activation/proliferation and NF-kappaB-dependent transcription and reduces TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-8, and VEGF.
Protease inhibitors cause prelamin A accumulation, oxidative stress, and premature senescence in human fibroblasts.
Ritonavir causes mitochondrial DNA damage and cytotoxicity in human endothelial cells, mainly via necrosis rather than apoptosis.
